title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Budget cut motion, doctor declaration
sections.summary: The speaker moves to reduce Head O of the Estimates by $100 and declares he is a public hospital doctor and son of a cancer patient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head O of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I declare that I am a medical doctor in a public hospital and I am the son of a cancer patient.

sections.label: Bedbound Ah Ma subsidy access
sections.summary: Ah Ma could not reach the polyclinic, so she paid unsubsidised rates and could not use her Pioneer Generation card; the speaker asks about the review's progress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Ah Ma was bedbound, not able to get out of the home, not able to physically get to the polyclinic nearby.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But when the prescription was brought to the polyclinic, she had to pay unsubsidised rates for her medicine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: She could not make use of her Pioneer Generation (PG) card because she was not physically able to get to the polyclinic, walk in the door, register as a subsidised patient, make use of that subsidy and the PG additional subsidy too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Minister Ong Ye Kung, last year, thanked my Clementi residents and I for pointing out "that healthcare subsidies should not be tied to services being delivered in brick-and-mortar facilities".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what is the progress of the review and what improvements are being looked at to support less mobile patients and seniors at home?

sections.label: Healthcare workers leaving and returning
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOH how many healthcare workers of working age left the workforce in the past five years and how many returned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can MOH tell us how many healthcare workers have left the workforce in the past five years, despite still being of working age?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And how many former healthcare workers have since returned to service in the last five years?

sections.label: Family doctors joining Healthier SG
sections.summary: The speaker asks what is being done to help family doctors come onboard Healthier SG, especially at older, non-digital clinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: On Healthier SG, what is being done to help family doctors come onboard, especially at older clinics which are not already digital?

sections.label: Consultation time saved on software
sections.summary: The speaker says 14 million consultations in 2019 mean one minute less on software per consultation would save 14 million minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2019, the last year before COVID-19, there were 14 million consultations across the healthcare system alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: If in each consultation, you spend one minute less navigating the software, making things happen on the computer, that is 14 million minutes saved – 14 million minutes of technical debt, 10,000 workdays or 27 years of someone working round the clock, 24 hours a day.

sections.label: Supply-induced demand in healthcare
sections.summary: The speaker notes healthcare economists talk about supply-induced demand, where patients in some countries are encouraged to use more healthcare resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Healthcare economists talk about "supply-induced demand" where in some countries, a patient might be encouraged to use more healthcare resources.

sections.label: Smoking cessation consultation length
sections.summary: Six five-minute consultations are not the same as a half-hour conversation about quitting smoking or changing lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Six consultations of five minutes each are not the same as a half-hour conversation, especially when speaking with someone about quitting smoking, changing a lifestyle to save someone's life.

sections.label: Excess deaths after infections subside
sections.summary: It asks what is driving excess deaths now that reported infection numbers are subsiding.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: What is driving excess deaths now that the reported infection numbers are subsiding?

sections.label: Gazetting essential supplies as state property
sections.summary: It asks whether MOH will work with MinLaw and AGC to study gazetting essential supplies as sovereign state property upon purchase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Learning from the lessons of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) protectionism where some countries imposed export bans, will MOH consider working with the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) and the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) to study whether certain essential supplies purchased by the Singapore Government can be gazetted as sovereign state property the moment the purchase is complete, even if the item is still in a overseas supplier's warehouse?

sections.label: Policy choices shape tomorrows
sections.summary: It states that policy choices today shape all our tomorrows, in sickness and in health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because our policy choices today shape all our tomorrows, in sickness and in health.

sections.label: Healthy longevity centres and clinic update
sections.summary: It asks for an update on using centres like NUS' Centre of Healthy Longevity and news on the Alexander Hospital longevity clinic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can the MOH provide an update on our attempts to utilise centres, such as NUS' Centre of Healthy Longevity, to extend the lifespan of our seniors and future generations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can the Minister give news about the upcoming longevity clinic at Alexander Hospital set to open this year?

sections.label: Ageing population and life expectancy
sections.summary: By 2030 one quarter of Singapore's population will be aged 65 and above, and life expectancy is expected to reach 85.4 by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2030, one quarter of Singapore's population will be aged 65 and above, and life expectancy currently of 83.9 will be expected to reach 85.4 by 2040.

sections.label: Healthier SG launch update
sections.summary: The MP asks the Minister for an update on the launch of Healthier SG, targeted for the middle of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: On this note, I would like to ask the Minister for an update on the launch of Healthier SG, which is targeted for the middle of this year.

sections.label: Singapore medical inflation
sections.summary: The MP asks what the current and projected medical inflation for Singapore is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What is the current and projected medical inflation for Singapore?

sections.label: Healthier SG budget and GP fees
sections.summary: The MP recounts the over $1 billion start-up budget, about $400 million annual recurrent expense, and half going to GPs as capitated service fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I asked at the Healthier SG White Paper debate on how the slightly over $1 billion start-up budget would be used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I was thankful that besides the broad allocation of this amount, which will include a chunk to upgrade the capabilities and IT capabilities of GPs, Minister Ong Ye Kung added that there will be a recurrent expense of about $400 million annually, of which half will go to GPs as their capitated service fee for looking after enrolled patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I did a probably highly inaccurate and overly simplistic back-of-the envelope estimate using $200 million annually, and assuming the total 1,250 GPs mentioned in MOH website on the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP) are to all participate in Healthier SG, noting that this number includes specialist outpatient clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This may still come up to about over $100,000 per GP annually.

sections.label: Telehealth exception permanence
sections.summary: The MP asks whether the time-limited exception should be made permanent so GPs can use more HealthTech solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is, given the advancement in telehealth to help increase productivity and enhance patient self-management, should this time-limited exception be made a permanent provision instead, so that GPs can innovate and utilise more proven HealthTech solutions?

sections.label: TCM role in Healthier SG
sections.summary: The MP hopes TCM is given a higher national role in keeping Singaporeans healthier, including in Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My residents in Jalan Kayu also benefited for decades from the highly affordable TCM services by Sian Chay Medical Institution, a charity with the Institution of Public Character (IPC) status approved by MOH.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I thus hope to see TCM being given a higher national role to play in keeping Singaporeans healthier, including in the Healthier SG initiative.

sections.label: VIFAP applications and rejections
sections.summary: The MP cites 413 VIFAP applications paid nearly $1.9 million as of 31 December 2022 and asks reasons for rejected applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOH has released information that as of 31 December 2022, 413 applications have received payments under VIFAP, with nearly $1.9 million having been paid out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Minister also let us know the reasons for turning down those applications?

sections.label: Rejected applicants daily living claims
sections.summary: The passage asks how many turned-down applicants claimed they were unable to perform activities of daily living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For those applicants who were turned down, how many of them claimed that they were unable to perform the activities of daily living?

sections.label: Singaporeans doing full-time caregiving
sections.summary: The passage states that over 210,000 Singaporeans do the full-time work of caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there are over 210,000 Singaporeans who do the full-time work of caregiving.

sections.label: Carefare for stay-home caregivers
sections.summary: The passage states Carefare is needed by stay-home caregivers from low-income families who give up jobs to care full-time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Carefare, as an income supplement, is needed by stay-home caregivers from low-income families, especially those who are forced by circumstances to give up their jobs and livelihoods to care full-time.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant eligibility and costs
sections.summary: The passage describes HCG amounts and income limits, cites a Duke-NUS study on informal caregiving costs, and proposes extending HCG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is now between $250 and $400 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, those who have a monthly household income per person of more than $2,800 do not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A study by researchers at Duke-NUS Medical School found that the cost of informal caregiving time for a care recipient who needs help with three or more Activities of Daily Living, or ADLs, is about $53,244 annually, or $4,437 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I propose that the Government extend the HCG to households earning up to the prevailing median income per household member?

sections.label: GPs and Drug Whitelist concerns
sections.summary: The passage states GPs are vital to Healthier SG but some are concerned about the Drug Whitelist and price caps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, working with GPs is a vital component of Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, some GPs are concerned about the proposed Drug Whitelist and the price caps for each drug in the whitelist.

sections.label: Affordable Assisted Living for seniors
sections.summary: The passage states that creating affordable Assisted Living services is needed to empower seniors to age-in-place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, to empower our seniors to age-in-place, we must spur the creation of affordable Assisted Living services.

sections.label: Assisted Living service sector roadmap
sections.summary: MOH must work across Government to plan Assisted Living services, fund infrastructure and services, and grow the number of AACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: MOH will need to work with various Ministries and agencies to map out the needs of our people, determine the optimal network design of such Assisted Living services in both public and private estates, so as to minimise the service provision cost, fund the infrastructure building and co-fund the service provision, help our seniors free up their assets to pay for their share of these services and to work with the private and people sector to spur the creation of a spectrum of services that will meet differing needs and budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Can the Minister for Health share his thinking on how these matters, especially on how it will work with the whole-of-Government to come up with a concrete roadmap, to spur the Assisted Living service sector for all?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: It plans to grow the number of AACs significantly.

sections.label: Healthier SG preventive-health pivot
sections.summary: A key to Healthier SG is pivoting from treating sickness to an upstream preventive-health approach for population-wide health management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, a key to the Healthier SG strategy is to pivot from just treating sickness when one is ill to an upstream preventive-health approach for a population-wide health management.

sections.label: Community nodes for healthier lifestyles
sections.summary: Strong community nodes and connectors are essential for Healthier SG, as Singaporeans live longer with higher disease prevalence and less family support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: As such, having strong nodes and connectors in the community to support and even conjure healthier lifestyles is essential for the full potential of Healthier SG to be reaped.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: This is important because Singaporeans are also living longer but facing challenges of higher disease prevalence and less family support, with seniors above 65 years old living alone or with a fellow senior having increased.

sections.label: Junior doctors and nurses working conditions
sections.summary: In the last two years there has been much press on bad working conditions of junior doctors and nurses in public healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, in the last two years, there has been much press on the bad working conditions of junior doctors and nurses in the public healthcare system.

sections.label: Retaining experienced healthcare staff
sections.summary: The passage asks what measures are in place to retain experienced staff, including those from foreign countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, what are the measures in place to retain experienced staff, including those from foreign countries?

sections.label: Work-life balance performance indicators
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry sets concrete performance indicators to measure junior doctors' and nurses' work-life balance, such as target average weekly working hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, are there concrete performance indicators that the Ministry sets to measure the work-life balance of junior doctors and nurses, for example, a target average number of working hours per week?

sections.label: Definition of abuse against healthcare workers
sections.summary: Asks whether all public health institutions have a standard definition of abuse against healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: To better protect our healthcare workers, I would like to ask if all the public health institutions have a standard definition of abuse against healthcare workers?

sections.label: MOH and law enforcement prosecution
sections.summary: Asks how MOH works with law enforcement agencies to prosecute abusers for serious cases under POHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Four, how is MOH working with the law enforcement agencies to prosecute abusers for serious cases under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA)?

sections.label: Future of long-term care paper
sections.summary: A Lee Kuan Yew School paper identified manpower capabilities, infrastructure capacity and sector coordination as three main issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A paper on the Future of Long-Term Care in Singapore by researchers from the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, identified three main issues to tackle in this sector – manpower capabilities, infrastructure capacity and coordination across the sector.

sections.label: ILTC reliance on foreign workers
sections.summary: Asks what plans MOH and ILTC providers have to encourage more Singaporeans to join the sector, and results so far.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Lien Foundation has pointed out that Singapore's ILTC sector is more reliant on foreign workers than other fast-ageing economies, such as Australia, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What plans do MOH and ILTC providers have, to encourage more Singaporeans to join the sector and what results have been achieved so far?

sections.label: Male registered nurses in 2021
sections.summary: States that only 12% of registered nurses in 2021 were males.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, only 12% of registered nurses in 2021 were males.

sections.label: Effects of workplace harassment on workers
sections.summary: Studies show harassed healthcare workers are more likely to face burnout, job dissatisfaction and emotional exhaustion, raising absenteeism and turnover.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that healthcare workers who experienced workplace harassment and abuse are more likely to experience burnout, job dissatisfaction and emotional exhaustion, leading to higher absenteeism and turnover rates.

sections.label: Disability rates and dental health
sections.summary: Singapore's disability rate is about 2.1% of students, 3.4% of those aged 18 to 49 and 13.3% of those 50 and above, and is expected to rise by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's disability rate is approximately 2.1% of the student population, 3.4% of those aged 18 to 49 years and 13.3% of those aged 50 and above.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2030, the number of individuals with disabilities is expected to significantly rise due to Singapore's ageing population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, a 2016 study revealed that only 9% of people aged 80 or older possess at least 20 teeth, while 30% of those aged 60 and above have no teeth at all.

sections.label: Geriatric and special care dentistry
sections.summary: Geriatric and special care dentistry are not recognised as a dental specialty, though both are crucial for access to quality care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Both are crucial to ensure all have access to quality care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, geriatric and special care dentistry are not recognised as a dental specialty.

sections.label: Recognising dental specialty urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to make geriatric and special care dentistry a recognised specialty, as lack of recognition may deter young dentists from training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may deter young dentists from getting this training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I strongly urge MOH to make it a recognised specialty.

sections.label: Speaker declares interests
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as a breast surgeon in private practice and as elected president of the Singapore Medical Association.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I declare my interest as a breast surgeon in private practice and my role as the elected president of the Singapore Medical Association (SMA).

sections.label: Barriers to patient care
sections.summary: The speaker finds more artificial barriers to real patient care, including third party administrators, insurance restrictions, the Cancer Drug List and reimbursement limits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The more senior I get, the more artificial barriers I find between me and real patient care: third party administrators, insurance restrictions; the Cancer Drug List (CDL); reimbursement limits for various schemes.

sections.label: Public education on healthcare system
sections.summary: The speaker asks for help with public education on navigating the local healthcare system and using health insurance plans, and intends to lead SMA with CASE.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Help us with public education: how to navigate the local healthcare system, how to best utilise your health insurance plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I intend to lead the SMA in collaboration with Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) to jump start this.

sections.label: Rejected GIA proposal
sections.summary: On 29 November 2022, he rejected a proposal by the General Insurance Association (GIA).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 29 November 2022, he rejected a proposal by the General Insurance Association (GIA).

sections.label: No final arbiter in IPs
sections.summary: He learnt the concept of "final arbiter" as a surgical trainee, and states there is no final arbiter in Integrated Shield Plans when clinical matters are involved.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Once again, I learnt something valuable from him, as I often had in the past as a surgical trainee – the concept of "final arbiter".

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is no final arbiter in Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) when clinical matters are involved.

sections.label: Clinical Claims Resolution Process questions
sections.summary: The voluntary CCRP, presented by the MHIC, falls apart if any party does not participate, and he asks MOH for annual updates on filed cases, cases that could not proceed, and refusing parties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, there is a Clinical Claims Resolution Process (CCRP), which was one of the solutions presented by the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (MHIC), of which I am an appointed member.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a platform with great potential, in which patients, IP providers and healthcare providers – both doctors and hospitals – can take part in when disputes arise due to clinical issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But the CCRP is a voluntary process and it falls apart when any one party does not wish to participate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will MOH consider annual updates on the number of CCRP cases that have been filed and, in addition, state how many cases could not proceed because one or more of these parties refused to take part, and who the refusing parties were?

sections.label: Expectations of Integrated Shield Plans
sections.summary: Sixty-five percent of Singaporeans have IPs, bought expecting private-sector treatment with chosen doctors, faster access and affordability when catastrophic disease strikes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sixty-five percent of Singaporeans have IPs, and we bought them with the expectation that when a catastrophic disease like cancer strikes us, we can proceed with treatment in the private sector where we get to choose the doctors that we are comfortable with, have faster access to treatments and be able to afford it.

sections.label: Out-of-pocket payments and subsidised care
sections.summary: If out-of-pocket payment exceeds, say, $3,000 a month for all services, a patient with private insurance may opt for subsidised care in a restructured hospital.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even with a Shield Plan, if the out-of-pocket payment exceeds, say, $3,000 a month, not just for drugs but for all services, such as consultation fees, investigations and non-cancer drugs to treat side effects of therapy, then perhaps this patient may opt for subsidised care in a restructured hospital, even though he or she has private insurance.

sections.label: Cancer care affordability and MOH study
sections.summary: He describes the double whammy of a cancer diagnosis and inadequate IP coverage, hopes MOH studies out-of-pocket payments for CDL versus non-CDL drugs, and poses issues and questions on affordability, expectations, resources and survival rates; he also states only NDCS and NUCOHS are referral centres providing the full range of subsidised dental services, while HDCs may provide medically indicated

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a tragic and stressful situation to have a double whammy of receiving a cancer diagnosis, and then finding out that they actually cannot afford cancer care in private because the IP coverage is inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope MOH can use existing bill sizes and conduct a large-scale study of the out-of-pocket payments for cancer treatment for IP policyholders under the new terms for CDL versus non-CDL drugs, should they opt for private healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I pose several issues for thought: (a) the insurance industry is heavily regulated and I respect their work; yet, I am mindful that they are business entities who need to be profitable, yet keep premiums affordable; (b) public expectations of what our IPs can cover have to be managed; (c) out-of-pocket payments by patients need to stay affordable; and (d) limited public healthcare resources have to be managed prudently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How many patients on private insurance will still not be able to pay for drugs and have to go to the restructured hospitals for care; and how many may never be able to afford the so-called "better medications"?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will this affect long-term cancer survival rates?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Currently, only our two National Specialty Dental Centres (NSCs), namely, the National Dental Centre Singapore (NDCS) and the National University Centre for Oral Health (NUCOHS), are referral centres that provide the full range of subsidised dental services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Hospital dental clinics (HDCs), which are essentially all other hospitals with a dental clinic, are only permitted to provide medically indicated subsidised dental services to hospital patients across inpatient, outpatient and day surgery settings.

sections.label: KTPH wisdom teeth subsidies
sections.summary: KTPH has service capacity and capability for wisdom teeth surgeries, which were previously subsidised there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: For example, in KTPH, there are service capacity and capability to handle wisdom teeth surgeries, and these were actually already previously subsidised in KTPH.

sections.label: Subsidised dental care access, PR costs
sections.summary: An elderly Yishun resident must travel to NDCS or NUCOHS for subsidised specialty dental care despite a nearby hospital dental clinic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: In another example, an elderly person living in Yishun in need of subsidised specialty dental care and treatment will have to travel to NDCS and NUCOHS, even though the nearby hospital that he goes to for medical care also has a dental clinic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Therefore, considering the close proximity of the current dental NSCs situated centrally, mainly NDCS and that National University Hospital (NUH), can the Ministry consider allowing all hospital dental clinics to provide specialised subsidised treatment, in order to better serve patients located in further geographical locations?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
sentences.text: Can MOH also explain why HDCs need to partner with NSCs to provide an expanded scope of subsidised services?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: I also have residents – citizens – with parents who are permanent residents (PRs) – worried about the healthcare costs for their parents because the difference in subsidies for PRs is around 30% for C2 and B2 Class wards, around the same for day surgeries, and usually even higher for outpatient clinic visits and standard drugs.

sections.label: Abortion gestational limits call
sections.summary: The speaker repeats a call to lower gestational limits to 22 weeks, noting Singapore is one of seven countries allowing elective termination after 20 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While I am heartened that pre-termination mandatory counselling has been made mandatory since 2015, I repeat my call for gestational limits to be lowered to 22 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of only seven countries at the moment that provide elective termination after 20 weeks and we see evidence of increasing foetal viability in recent years, with improvements in medical care.

sections.label: Egg freezing age limit
sections.summary: The decision to fix the upper age limit for egg freezing at 35 may be well-grounded in scientific and medical arguments.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The decision to fix the upper age limit for egg freezing at 35 may be well‐grounded in scientific and medical arguments.

sections.label: NEHR clinic access
sections.summary: As of April 2022, all MOH polyclinics and almost 60% of private medical clinics have access to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: As of April 2022, all MOH polyclinics and almost 60% of private medical clinics have access to NEHR, but we should get more of these clinics to sign up.

sections.label: Healthier SG digital tracking
sections.summary: Healthier SG will let citizens follow personalised health plans on HealthHub and track physical activities on the Healthy 365 app.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: The Healthier SG plan will allow citizens to follow their personalised health plans on HealthHub and track their physical activities on the Healthy 365 app.

sections.label: Mental health task force recommendations
sections.summary: The Interagency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being proposed 12 preliminary recommendations in three focus areas last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: Last year, the Interagency Task Force on Mental Health and Well-being proposed 12 preliminary recommendations in three focus areas.

sections.label: Vaping and smoking cases
sections.summary: HSA handled 2,477 vaping cases in 2019, rising to 7,593 in 2021, with about seven in 1,000 public school students caught over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: HSA dealt with 2,477 cases of vaping in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: The number increased by three times to 7,593 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Over the past three years, an average of about seven out of 1,000 students from a public school were caught for smoking and vaping offences.

sections.label: Vape fines
sections.summary: Purchase, usage or ownership of an electronic vape may result in fines of up to $2,000 per offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Lastly, I understand the purchase, usage or ownership of an electronic vape may result in fines of up to $2,000 per offence.

sections.label: Death rate and programme distribution
sections.summary: The age standardised death rate rose from 549.9 at end-June 2022 to 555.7 at end-December 2022, an excess of 30.7 per 100,000 person years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Also, how does the Ministry plan to ensure that these programmes remain well-distributed across various locations, so that residents in every neighbourhood continue to have easy access to this physical activity programmes?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I reported in the House late last year that as at end-June 2022, our age standardised death rate throughout the pandemic was 549.9, per 100,000 person years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As at end December 2022, the number has gone up further and slightly to 555.7.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is expected as we are taking in the mortality of all major infection waves throughout the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This indicates an excess death rate of 30.7 per 100,000 person years.

sections.label: Nurse and care staff increase
sections.summary: Projections require increasing nurses and support care staff by about 40%, from 49,000 now to 69,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But let me make a few comments first.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need, based on our projections, to increase the number of nurses and support care staff by about 40% – from 49,000 now, to 69,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Abuse of healthcare workers
sections.summary: Abuse and harassment by a small minority is a rising issue in Singapore's healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is hugely motivating for our healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: But abuse and harassment by a small minority is a rising issue in our healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Public hospital beds increase
sections.summary: About 11,000 public hospital beds exist today, with 1,900 more planned over five years, mainly from Woodlands Health Campus starting end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Third, we also need to improve the support system and safety net for vulnerable groups, especially to the lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We have about 11,000 public hospital beds today and we intend to add 1,900 more public hospital beds over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This will mainly come from Woodlands Health Campus which we are waiting eagerly for, and this will progressively start operations from end of this year.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment for seniors
sections.summary: Healthier SG enrolment for Singaporeans aged 60 and above will launch in July this year, with most hoped to become partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We hope to secure the great majority of them to be our partners in Healthier SG eventually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I announced last week that we will launch the Healthier SG enrolment for Singaporeans aged 60 and above in July this year.

sections.label: First Healthier SG benefits tranche
sections.summary: From July 2023, the first tranche of Healthier SG benefits will kick in.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: From July 2023, the first tranche of Healthier SG benefits will also kick in.

sections.label: Second Healthier SG benefits tranche
sections.summary: In early 2024, a second tranche of benefits requiring more operational preparation will kick in.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In early 2024, a second tranche of benefits, which will require more operational preparation, will kick in.

sections.label: Chronic drugs at GP clinics
sections.summary: Under Healthier SG, patients may get polyclinic chronic drugs at Healthier SG GP clinics at around the same price, via a new CHAS Chronic Tier subsidy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under Healthier SG, this group of patients has the choice to get their supply of polyclinic chronic drugs at Healthier SG GP clinics at around the same price as polyclinic drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is because we will provide a new Healthier SG CHAS Chronic Tier subsidy for selected drugs.

sections.label: Removal of cash co-payment
sections.summary: Another benefit is the removal of cash co-payment when using MediSave for chronic treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Another benefit is the removal of cash co-payment when using MediSave for chronic treatment.

sections.label: Nursing home capacity expansion
sections.summary: Nursing home capacity is doubling from 16,000 in 2020 to over 31,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Several Members of Parliament have asked about this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are building many more nursing homes, doubling from 16,000 in 2020, to over 31,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Support for AACs
sections.summary: MOH is studying how best to strengthen support to AACs, potentially a major healthcare programme alongside Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MOH is studying how best to strengthen our support to AACs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is, potentially, another major healthcare programme, alongside Healthier SG.

sections.label: Healthcare Services (Amendment) Bill
sections.summary: The Healthcare Services (Amendment) Bill will be presented at the end of the COS debate for healthcare services delivered in various settings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need them for wherever healthcare services are delivered, including senior centres in the community, residential homes, mobile clinics or even remotely, via telemedicine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That is one of the key purposes of the Healthcare Services (Amendment) Bill, which we will present to the House at the end of the COS debate.

sections.label: MediSave for homebound patients
sections.summary: In the second half of this year, MediSave use will be extended to homebound patients receiving home medical care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: He put up a compelling case on why financing schemes need to be premises-neutral – to support patients like Ah Ma, who is immobile, homebound and finds it challenging to visit the polyclinic or the hospitals and, therefore, they have to rely on home care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, in the second half of this year, we will extend the use of MediSave to homebound patients receiving home medical care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They will be able to tap on the MediSave500/700 and Flexi-MediSave schemes.

sections.label: Telehealth policy not lapsing
sections.summary: The time-bound pandemic telehealth policy will not lapse under DORSCON Green because telehealth is widely accepted and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And this policy was meant to be time-bound, effective only during the period of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Now that we are in Disease Outbreak Response System Condition (DORSCON) Green, we will not lapse it because telehealth has become widely accepted and has demonstrated to be effective.

sections.label: Bundled hospice funding pilot
sections.summary: Three hospice funding formulas and streams will be bundled into one per patient funding rate, piloted with Dover Park Hospice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the same time, instead of having three funding formulas and three funding streams for different hospice settings – home, day, inpatient – we can bundle them into one per patient funding rate, set it at an adequate level and then empower the hospice to decide which settings are most suitable, depending on the care needs of the patients, and also their family circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We will pilot this new approach with Dover Park Hospice, which is working closely with TTSH.

sections.label: Enrolment and free vaccinations
sections.summary: From July, Singaporeans aged 60 and above are invited to enrol, receiving a $20 award and free annual vaccination and health screening.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Starting from July this year, we will invite Singaporeans aged 60 and above to enrol into the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: After the first consultation, the Government will provide an award worth $20.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Subsequently, annual vaccination and health screening as recommended by MOH will also be free-of-charge.

sections.label: MediSave for home medical care
sections.summary: In the second half of this year, the policy will be adjusted so this group of patients can use MediSave for home medical care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the second half of this year, we will adjust the policy, so that this group of patients can use MediSave for home medical care to reduce their medical burden.

sections.label: Mainstream healthcare incorporation
sections.summary: If all goes well, the arrangement is expected to be incorporated into the mainstream healthcare system next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: If all goes well, we expect to incorporate such an arrangement into our mainstream healthcare system next year.

sections.label: Frontier medical science costs
sections.summary: Frontier medical science reported in the media is usually not suitable for most patients, and unwise development can cost the country a lot.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: While these get reported in the media, they usually are not suitable for the majority of patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, if we are not wise or careful in the development of frontier medical science, the country can end up paying a lot, including wiping out savings of many people, for very little good outcomes.

sections.label: Personal responsibility and co-payment
sections.summary: The system must emphasise personal responsibility, so co-payment of medical bills and insurance payouts remain an important principle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Therefore, the system must be designed with an emphasis on personal responsibility, to ensure prudence and discipline in spending on sickness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And that is why co-payment of medical bills and insurance payouts remain an important principle of our system.

sections.label: Healthier SG preventive care
sections.summary: Through Healthier SG, preventive care like nationally recommended health screenings and vaccinations is made free, like public parks and libraries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This is the driving force behind the healthcare transformation that we are witnessing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, through Healthier SG, we have decided to make preventive care like nationally recommended health screenings and vaccinations to be like public parks and libraries – all over and free.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We need to invest in infrastructure and systems that keep people healthy, just as we do for public transport and clean water.

sections.label: Mature multifaceted healthcare system
sections.summary: A more mature and multifaceted healthcare system spanning frontier, biological and social sciences is needed for an ageing population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Today, we need a more mature and multifaceted healthcare system, three systems in fact – spanning frontier, biological and social sciences – so as to provide for the more complex needs and opportunities of an ageing population.

sections.label: Family Nexus pilot rollout
sections.summary: The first Family Nexus pilot has been rolled out at Our Tampines Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, I announced that we were piloting this programme, which we call Family Nexus.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am pleased to update that the first Family Nexus pilot has since been rolled out at Our Tampines Hub (OTH).

sections.label: Family Nexus expansion sites
sections.summary: Family Nexus hubs will be rolled out to Choa Keang, Punggol and Sembawang.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Integrated hubs like FamNex@OTH will be rolled out to more sites across Singapore, at Choa Chu Kang and Punggol, supporting more families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Family Nexus@ Sembawang will also be ready when the new Sembawang Polyclinic opens at Bukit Canberra later this year.

sections.label: Mother-child dyad polyclinics
sections.summary: Nine polyclinics offer mother-child dyad services, up from two a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Today, there are nine polyclinics which offer mother-child dyad services, an increase from the two polyclinics a year ago.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We will roll out these services to several more polyclinics by the end of this year and are ahead of our target to scale these services to 14 polyclinics by 2025.

sections.label: Maternal mental health programme
sections.summary: KKH has implemented the Psychological Resilience in Antenatal Management since last December.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Similarly, early identification and intervention are key to support maternal mental health.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, I am pleased to learn that KKH has implemented the Psychological Resilience in Antenatal Management since last December.

sections.label: Screen use advisory launch
sections.summary: An advisory on screen use for children aged zero to 12 years old is launched.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To provide more practical help to parents, I am pleased to launch the advisory on screen use for children aged zero to 12 years old.

sections.label: Supporting fathers' mental well-being
sections.summary: NUH will extend mental health screening and support to fathers of children and husbands of women under its care.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, it is important that we support the mental well-being of fathers too, to keep them well.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that NUH will be extending its mental health screening and support to fathers of children and husbands of women under its care.

sections.label: Support for lower-income families
sections.summary: HPB and partners will run two regional pilots in the Northeast and West to help lower-income families access health services and wraparound support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last year, HPB worked with community partners, such as PA, M3@Towns and Community Link (ComLink), to proactively reach out to lower-income families with young children, supporting them with resources and encouragement to facilitate healthier lifestyle choices, such as buying groceries with healthier choice symbol and engaging in regular physical exercises.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This year, we will be enhancing efforts to support lower-income families through two regional pilots, in collaboration with social agencies and preschools, supporting these families in accessing health services and providing wraparound support for both parents and children.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In the Northeast region, SingHealth will lead cross-domain and multi-agency efforts to support children from low-income families through Project HOME (Holistic Management and Enablement).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Healthcare agencies like Sengkang Hospital (SKH), KKH, Punggol polyclinic will partner My First Campus preschools as well as social services centres, the SSOs and FSCs to jointly support case management of children under six years old.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: A similar pilot will be rolled out in the West by NUH through the HEADS-UPP, or HEAlth and Development SUpport in Preschool Partnerships, programme.

sections.label: Caregiver Support Action Plan
sections.summary: The 2019 Caregiver Support Action Plan outlined initiatives in financial support, respite care, caregiver empowerment, workplace support and care navigation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 2019, we introduced the Caregiver Support Action Plan that outlined key initiatives in the areas of financial support, respite care, caregiver empowerment, workplace support and care navigation.

sections.label: Enhanced monthly payouts
sections.summary: From this month, eligible recipients will receive enhanced payouts of $400 or $250 per month, up from $200, with more support for lower income.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From this month, those who are eligible will start receiving enhanced payouts of either $400 or $250 per month, up from the current $200, with more support provided to the lower income.

sections.label: Expanding Household Services Scheme
sections.summary: MOM will expand the Household Services Scheme to provide basic child-minding and elder-minding services for families with lighter caregiving needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For those families with lighter caregiving needs, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has earlier shared that it will expand the scope of the Household Services Scheme (HSS) to provide basic child-minding and elder-minding services.

sections.label: Data contribution to NEHR
sections.summary: Licensed healthcare providers will be required and selected entities allowed to contribute data to the NEHR, with Healthier SG GPs required within one year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To support these initiatives and many others, we will require our licensed healthcare providers and allow selected entities to contribute data to the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: GPs participating in Healthier SG will be required to contribute to the NEHR within one year from the launch.

sections.label: New Health Information Bill
sections.summary: New legislation, the Health Information Bill, will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To achieve all this, we will be introducing new legislation, the Health Information Bill.

sections.label: Health data collection and sharing
sections.summary: The Bill enables collecting patients' selected health data, sharing health and administrative data, and governing collection, use and disclosure with cybersecurity and data security requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: First, to enable the collection of patients' selected health data from healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Second, to allow healthcare providers to share health and administrative data with one another for specific purposes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And three – and third, I beg your pardon, to govern the collection, use and disclosure of such data by setting out robust cybersecurity and data security requirements.

sections.label: Bill tabling later this year
sections.summary: Consultations continue and feedback will be addressed, with the Bill intended to be tabled later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The consultations continue and we will address the feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We subsequently intend to table the Bill in this House in the later part of this year.

sections.label: Elective egg freezing donor age limit
sections.summary: The upper age limit of donors for elective egg freezing, implemented in June 2023, is presently 35 years of age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In response to Miss Cheng Li Hui, the upper age limit of donors for elective egg freezing, which will be implemented in June 2023, is presently set at 35 years of age.

sections.label: Cancer drugs share of drug spending
sections.summary: Cancer patients account for about 2% of all patients, while cancer drugs make up 35% of public sector drug spending.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Although cancer patients account for about 2% of all patients, cancer drugs make up 35% of public sector drug spending.

sections.label: CDL price reduction and patient uptake
sections.summary: Since 2021, the CDL helped MOH secure an average 30% price reduction on listed drugs, with most patients on CDL treatments from September to December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since its announcement in 2021, the CDL has helped MOH secure an average price reduction of 30% on the listed drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: From 1 September to 31 December 2022, an average of 90% of patients in private medical institutions and about 95% of patients in Public Healthcare Institutions were on CDL treatments.

sections.label: VIFAP applications and clinical panel
sections.summary: As of 31 January 2023, MOH received 2,405 VIFAP applications with 414 payouts, reviewed by an independent clinical panel.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2023, MOH has received 2,405 applications, with 414 payouts made.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: VIFAP applications are reviewed and assessed by an independent VIFAP clinical panel, which includes senior specialists in the relevant fields of neurology, immunology and allergy, and infectious diseases.

sections.label: VIFAP reassessment of applications
sections.summary: The VIFAP panel assesses applications and considers new evidence, with 24 applications successfully reassessed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The VIFAP panel will assess the application and consider the new evidence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: There have been 24 applications that were successfully reassessed.

sections.label: Task force mental health recommendations
sections.summary: The task force preliminarily identified 12 recommendations in three areas, receiving over 950 responses from various groups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The task force has preliminarily identified 12 recommendations focused on three areas: (a) improving the accessibility, coordination and quality of mental health services; (b) strengthening services and support for youth mental well-being; and (c) improving workplace well-being measures and employment support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Over 950 responses were received, with feedback from groups, such as youths, parents, persons with mental health conditions, service providers, employers and community agencies.

sections.label: Youth suicide prevention guidelines
sections.summary: IMH partnered SOS and is developing guidelines for youth suicide prevention programmes as a resource for service providers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In the last example, the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) has partnered the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) and are in the midst of developing a set of guidelines for youth suicide prevention programmes as a resource for service providers.

sections.label: National mental health competency framework
sections.summary: Task force representatives from social, health and education sectors developed a national mental health competency training framework to guide practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Task force representatives from the social, health and education sectors have come together to develop a national mental health competency training framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The framework will establish a structured approach to guide mental health practitioners in developing the knowledge, skills and competencies necessary to deliver high-quality and effective care.

sections.label: National mental health strategy development
sections.summary: The task force will continue its mandate toward a national mental health strategy by year-end and explore coordination options like a central office.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The task force will continue to carry out its mandate and work towards the development of a national strategy for mental health and well-being aimed to be released by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will also continue to explore other options to coordinate national efforts on mental health and well-being, such as considering the value of establishing a central coordination office.

sections.label: Allied health graduate intake increase
sections.summary: The first batch of 230 allied health graduates entered the workforce in 2020, and after an intake increase of about 85%, about 430 students from the 2022 batch will enter in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, the first batch of 230 allied health graduates from the Singapore Institute of Technology entered the workforce in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: After increasing the intake by around 85%, about 430 students from the 2022 batch will enter the workforce in 2026.

sections.label: Nurse attrition rates
sections.summary: Local nurse attrition stayed stable from 2019 to 2022, while foreign nurse attrition rose from 9.5% to 14.5% over the same period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The attrition rate for local nurses has remained stable over 2019 to 2022, but, for foreign nurses, this has spiked from 9.5% to 14.5% over the same period.

sections.label: Nurse return and non-renewal numbers
sections.summary: Over the past five years, about 750 non-practising nurses returned yearly, joining some 2,400 new nurses, while about 1,300 nurses did not renew certificates each year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Every year, over the past five years, about 750 non-practising nurses return to practice, joining some 2,400 new nurses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In comparison, about 1,300 nurses do not renew their practicing certificates each year.

sections.label: Healthcare staff well-being measures
sections.summary: Public healthcare clusters appointed Chief Wellness Officers, support counselling and peer networks, review administrative processes for rest, and are reviewing junior doctors' working hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In recent years, the public healthcare clusters have appointed Chief Wellness Officers to develop system changes to improve staff well-being and also support measures like counselling and peer support networks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To ensure healthcare workers have enough rest between and during shifts, the clusters regularly review administrative processes and remove them if not needed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are also reviewing the working hours of junior doctors, but it is a complex issue that will take time to work out.

sections.label: Abuse of healthcare workers
sections.summary: Almost one in three healthcare workers witnessed or experienced abuse at least weekly, and steps include improving and standardising how public healthcare institutions deal with abuse and harassment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Almost one in three healthcare workers have witnessed or experienced abuse at least once a week.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We need to take decisive steps to ensure the safety and well-being of our healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This includes enhancing protection for healthcare workers by improving and standardising how public healthcare institutions deal with abuse and harassment.

sections.label: Malay and Indian healthy living participation
sections.summary: In the past year or so, over 29,000 Malay residents and over 32,000 Indian residents participated in healthy living programmes like exercise and mental well-being workshops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In the past year or so, over 29,000 Malay residents and over 32,000 Indian residents have participated in healthy living programmes, like exercise and mental well-being workshops.

sections.label: Our Healthy Singapore Fund proposals
sections.summary: HPB and MCCY's $1.5 million Our Healthy Singapore Fund received almost 50 proposals between April and December last year, with seven awarded so far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Last year, I shared that HPB is partnering MCCY to establish a $1.5 million fund, Our Healthy Singapore Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This fund empowers community volunteers and organisations to kickstart ground-up health promotion initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that between April and December last year, we received almost 50 proposals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are in the midst of evaluation and have awarded seven proposals so far.

sections.label: Daily smoking prevalence 2022
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2022 shows daily smoking prevalence stable at 9.2%, with a long-term goal of a nicotine-free Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Based on the latest National Population Health Survey 2022, the prevalence of daily smoking remains stable at 9.2%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We remain committed to our long-term goal to bring the overall smoking rate to a level that is as low as possible, and ultimately, to pursue a nicotine-free Singapore.

sections.label: Parents, vaping and nicotine-free Singapore
sections.summary: Parents are urged to talk to children about smoking and vaping, while efforts continue on tobacco control, vaping penalties, enforcement and preventive health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We hope that parents can have a serious conversation with their children about smoking and vaping and to do it soon, before it becomes a life-long habit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will continue to work towards a nicotine-free Singapore by exploring next-bound efforts of the tobacco control strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will also continue to enhance our strategy to address the issue of vaping, including reviewing legislated penalties, enhancing enforcement, deterrence and education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Ministry continues to strengthen upstream preventive health efforts, but Singaporeans must do their part to make healthier choices and lead healthier lifestyles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Programmes may come with incentives like Healthpoints and that is useful to help us get started.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, what we are nudging Singaporeans towards – the real reward that matters – which are the positive health outcomes of embracing a healthy lifestyle.

sections.label: Complaints about misleading medical claims
sections.summary: A claim to treat an identifiable medical disease like cancer would be a misleading claim the public could complain about.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: Thirdly, whom may the public lodge a complaint with?

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Certainly, if the claim is to treat an identifiable medical disease like cancer, that would be a misleading claim.

sections.label: Licensed providers and provable claims
sections.summary: Ongoing public education is needed because medical treatment changes, and licensed providers must assert only provable and demonstrable claims.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is going to have to require ongoing efforts around public education because medical treatment does change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I think the key issue is that if the provider is licensed, they are required only to assert claims that are provable and demonstrable.

sections.label: Telehealth support and remote monitoring
sections.summary: Telehealth support would be extended so long as it is appropriate and efficacious, and remote apparatus allows monitoring without charge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On telehealth, the short answer is, so long as it is appropriate, efficacious, we would like to extend the support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you have the remote apparatus, you can monitor without charge.

sections.label: HCG qualifying income pegging
sections.summary: The HCG qualifying income is pegged to median income based on DOS statistics, excluding employer CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In any case, can the HCG qualifying income be pegged to the median income?

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: It is pegged to the median income based on DOS' statistics, but it does not include the Central Provident Fund (CPF) contribution of the employer.

sections.label: Doctor and nurse attrition
sections.summary: Doctor and local nurse attrition stayed stable during the pandemic, though it jumped to 14% from a steady 7% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Actually, the attrition of doctors and local nurses has been stable throughout the pandemic, despite the very hard, very heavy workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think from 7%, 8% or 9%, which was at steady state, it jumped to 14% during the pandemic.

sections.label: Increase from 49,000 to 69,000
sections.summary: The number is to be increased from 49,000 to 69,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I mentioned just now, from 49,000, we want to increase to 69,000 by 2030.

sections.label: One in 20 chose healthcare
sections.summary: In every cohort, one in 20 new students chose healthcare, and the majority are nurses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The number of new students per cohort, in every cohort, one in 20 chose healthcare and the majority are nurses.

sections.label: Shrinking cohorts and foreign nurses
sections.summary: If intake is kept and shrinking cohorts continue, the ratio may exceed one in 20, so the foreign nursing workforce must be beefed up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If we keep our intake and the cohort sizes start to shrink, it is starting to shrink, it may well go up beyond one in 20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we are getting our fair share, but we need to beef up to replace and expand our foreign nursing workforce.

sections.label: Healthy 365 app sign-ups
sections.summary: Plans are sought to get Singaporeans to sign up for the Healthy 365 app, with an option to give vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
sentences.text: What are the plans now to beef up to get Singaporeans to sign up for the Healthy 365 app?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think there is an option to give vouchers.

sections.label: Silver Generation Ambassadors sign-ups
sections.summary: Silver Generation Ambassadors will be mobilised to help people sign up for Healthier SG and Healthy 365.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is one way to get it kickstarted because we do know that if you hold a carnival, people do come down, participate and we will have ambassadors – we will mobilise all our Silver Generation Ambassadors who were very useful when we rolled out the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation packages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Now we can leverage their network to help people sign up for Healthier SG and also sign up for Healthy 365.

sections.label: Medical data and Singpass access
sections.summary: Summary health data is accessed using Singpass with high security and will be shared when the Health Information Bill is passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Your medical data, summary health data, is in there and you should access it using Singpass and have sufficiently high security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But it will also be shared when the Health Information Bill is passed by this House.

sections.label: National mental health competency framework
sections.summary: Professional bodies will develop a national mental health competency framework for shared language and standards, rather than a single regulatory framework.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: So, we need to ensure accountability, especially if things go wrong and we need it to be carried out properly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, the process is to bring the professional bodies together through the representatives that are participating in this approach to develop the national mental health competency framework and, through that, have the same language, and then the same high standards applied across all the different professional bodies, rather than try, at this point in time, to create a single regulatory framework for these sets of conditions.

sections.label: Nursing homes providing respite care
sections.summary: 60 nursing homes currently provide temporary respite care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Currently, there are 60 nursing homes already providing the temporary respite care.

sections.label: Thanks to pandemic frontliners
sections.summary: Thanks were given to the Multi-Ministry Task Force, officeholders, frontliners, healthcare workers and public officers for getting through the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, if I may beg your indulgence, through you, may I say a big thank you to our Multi-Ministry Task Force, Ministers, Senior Ministers of State, Senior Parliamentary Secretary, a very big thank you to our frontliners, healthcare workers, public officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Your strength and effort got us through the pandemic and to a new normal, a new dawn coloured in DORSCON Green.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The speaker begs leave to withdraw his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
